title: Approximate Machine Unlearning through Manifold Representation Forgetting Guided by Self Mode Connectivity

problem.claim: Machine unlearning is needed to enforce the right to be forgotten.

gap.claim: Existing label-manipulation and task-gradient-reversal approaches may have limited unlearning effectiveness, can undermine the original learning objective, and typically do not guarantee equivalence to retraining.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes ManiF-SMC, an approximate unlearning method based on manifold forgetting and self mode connectivity.
It reformulates approximate unlearning as moving erased samples away from their original representation centroids toward nearest semantic neighbors in retained data.
It uses a margin-based triplet loss and a self-mode-connectivity module to reconstruct a local manifold and generate adaptive unlearning margins.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four representative datasets reportedly show unlearning effectiveness comparable to state-of-the-art approximate methods.
The method reportedly operates solely within the model's representation space.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames machine unlearning as a mechanism for the right to be forgotten and identifies limitations in existing approaches.
The authors introduce ManiF-SMC based on retraining-like semantic behavior for erased samples.
Approximate unlearning is recast as representation-space movement toward semantic neighbors in retained data.
A margin-based triplet loss combines unlearning and representation preservation goals.
Self mode connectivity guides adaptive margins, followed by reported results across four datasets.

source_observation.claim: The method aligns approximate unlearning with retraining behavior by using semantic neighbors and representation-space objectives.

interpretation.claim: Unlearning objectives may be more transferable when expressed through representation geometry rather than task-specific labels or gradients.

application.claim: Approximate unlearning designs can consider semantic-neighbor constraints in representation space.

exception.claim: Margin selection remains challenging and requires adaptive guidance in this approach.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the four datasets, evaluation metrics, or comparison methods.
The abstract does not establish formal equivalence to retraining.
The abstract omits implementation details, hyperparameters, and computational costs.
